# Big Arrow

A skill that teaches an agent to use the bigarrow command line tool on macOS: draw a large click-through arrow with a written sign at a UI element, a window, a tab or a screen coordinate, whenever the human has to look at, click, type into or choose a specific spot. The sign is one full sentence naming the action, and for an approving, granting, paying, signing, sending or deleting click it also states what happens; a value to paste rides on the sign as a copy button. The arrow never takes the focus and never clicks, types or captures anything itself: the human clicks. It can speak the sign with --say for time-critical moments, and it ends on its own after a timeout, on bigarrow stop, or when the human answers if the optional hook is installed. The drawing itself needs no macOS permission; element and window targeting use the Accessibility permission of the terminal app, and Screen Recording for window titles on newer macOS. It needs the bigarrow binary 0.4.6 or newer, installed separately with Homebrew, on macOS only.
